rules.rule_5_reservation: Reservation as per State Government orders issued from time to time

eligible_candidates: Tibetan refugee who came to India before 1 January 1962 with intention to permanently settle
Person of Indian origin migrated from Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka or East African countries (Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania) intending to permanently settle in India
notes: Category (b) and (c) candidates require eligibility certificate from State Government
Category (b) also requires certificate from Deputy Inspector General of Police, Intelligence Branch, Uttarakhand
Category (c) certificate valid for not more than one year; candidate retained in service only if Indian citizenship obtained within that period

Obtained B or C certificate of National Cadet Corps

rule_10_age_limit.reference_date: 1st July of the calendar year vacancies are advertised
rule_10_age_limit.relaxation: Upper age relaxation for SC, ST, OBC and other notified categories as specified

rule_11_character.requirement: Character must render the candidate suitable for Government service
disqualified: Persons dismissed by Union/State Government, local authority or Government-owned corporation
Persons convicted of offence involving moral turpitude
Male with more than one living wife
Female who married a man already having a living wife or who has more than one living husband
rule_12_marital_status.exception: Government may exempt if satisfied specific grounds exist

rule_13_recruitment_procedure.sub_rule_1: Application format published on Commission website and in at least two widely circulated daily newspapers
rule_13_recruitment_procedure.sub_rule_2: Vacancies notified via: Commission website and newspapers; office notice board and radio/TV/employment journals; Employment Exchange
rule_13_recruitment_procedure.sub_rule_4: Candidates must undergo prescribed physical test; only those meeting minimum physical standards proceed to Physical Efficiency Test
rule_13_recruitment_procedure.physical_efficiency_test: Candidates up to 10 times the number of vacancies declared qualified for written exam
rule_13_recruitment_procedure.sub_rule_5: Physical Standards and Physical Efficiency Test carry 100 marks total

sub_rule_6_written_exam.marking: 1 mark per correct answer; 1/4 negative marking per wrong answer
sub_rule_6_written_exam.syllabus: Prepared by Commission/Selection Institution with Government approval

rule_13_recruitment_procedure.sub_rule_7: Candidates allowed to retain question booklet after exam
rule_13_recruitment_procedure.sub_rule_8: Answer sheet in duplicate with carbon copy; duplicate copy retained by candidate
rule_13_recruitment_procedure.sub_rule_9: Answer key published on Commission/Selection Institution website after exam

tie_breaking: Higher marks in written exam placed higher
If written exam marks also equal, elder candidate placed higher
If age also equal, preference as per Rule 9

rules.rule_14_examination_fee: As prescribed by Government/Selection Institution from time to time; no refund

rule_15_publication_of_marks.sub_rule_1: Marks of selected candidates published on website and displayed on notice board after selection list forwarded to Appointing Authority
rule_15_publication_of_marks.sub_rule_2: Total marks of all candidates displayed in descending order on website

rules.rule_16_saving: Rules shall not affect reservations and concessions for SC, ST, OBC, EWS and other categories as per Government orders
rules.rule_17_power_to_remove_difficulties: State Government may issue general or special orders to remove any difficulty in implementation

notifications.title: Uttarakhand On-Demand (Information Technology Based) Transportation by Contract Carriage (Amendment) Rules, 2024
notifications.act_under: Section 93, 95 and 96 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
notifications.principal_rules_amended: Uttarakhand On-Demand (Information Technology Based) Transportation by Contract Carriage Rules, 2020
notifications.effective_date: Date of publication in Official Gazette

definitions_added_or_amended.new_definition: Any license issued or renewed under Rule 6 to engage in on-demand transport by contract carriage which includes two and three wheeler vehicles based on information technology for hire or reward.
A service provider or operator who acts as a digital intermediary or market place for connecting a passenger with the operator or driver of a contract carriage under the Act.
An electronic interface operated by the Aggregator or any third party on behalf of the Aggregator, accessible through a computer resource or communication device.
The area or route permitted to operate in accordance with the permit to a contract carriage operated under these rules.
The payment made by the Aggregator to the Rider at the end of the journey after the Passenger has booked the fare displayed through the App.
An algorithm resulting from an aggregator that automatically increases the fare for a trip when demand in a given geographic area exceeds the supply.

key_rule_changes.change: Security deposit requirement changed from fixed Rs. 10 lakh bank guarantee to security in the form of bank guarantee, fixed deposit etc. of a scheduled bank with validity of five and a half years.

Applicant entity expanded from 'registered entity under applicable laws' to include companies under Companies Act 1956/2013, cooperative societies, LLPs, or any business undertaking formed under any law in force in India or any State. Fleet requirement changed from 50 motor cabs to 10 contract buses or 25 other vehicles.
Application window changed. Security deposit requirement updated to prescribed form in Rule 18.
Tracking device must comply with AIS 140 standard (Rule 125(h) of CMVR 1989). Location tracking device must comply with commands given by Licensing Authority through OTA or other means.

Aggregator must establish an induction training system for drivers. Mandatory 30-hour, 5-day training programme before on-boarding. Curriculum includes: efficient use of aggregator app; MV Act 1988 provisions; 6 hours road safety and first responder training; vehicle operation; cleaning and maintenance; routes; contract terms; gender sensitivity and protection of women and girls.

App must be made under IT Act 2000; in Hindi and English; security certified by accredited security association; internal vulnerabilities exposed to CERT-In; data stored for minimum 3 months and maximum 24 months; data provided to State Transport Authority as per prescribed procedure; no data displayed without written consent of customers.

Fare policy must be based on State Government rate. Proven software algorithm for fare and distance calculation, quality tested by STQC or MeitY-authorized institution. Minimum fare for first 5 km chargeable. Surge pricing maximum 25% above prescribed fare; if supply exceeds demand, up to 25% less than prescribed fare. Driver receives minimum 80% of fare per journey. 2% surcharge on each fare deposited to fund under Section 8A of Motor Vehicle Taxation (Reforms) Act 2003.

If booking cancelled by driver/vehicle owner/aggregator without valid reason: penalty 10% of total fare, max Rs. 200. If cancelled by rider without valid reason: penalty 10% of total fare, max Rs. 200, distributed 80:20 between driver and aggregator. All fines deposited in fund under Rule 8A(6).
License authority may suspend/revoke and forfeit total amount of security deposit or appropriate part thereof in case of malpractice or misconduct with passenger.

License can be transferred on joint application in Form 4 with fee per Rule 18. Transferee furnishes security till date of validity per Rule 18. Transferor's security returned after transfer. All terms and conditions apply to transferee as original licensee. Within 45 days of transfer, digital consent from all registered vehicles required.

Aggregators with fleet of not more than 500 two-wheelers and three-wheelers are exempt from clauses (x), (xi), (xiii), (xiv) of sub-rule (1) of Rule 8 and clause (v)(f) of sub-rule (3) of Rule 8 and Rule 8B. Ambulance category vehicles do not need separate license.

New fee table: (a) Fleet up to 500 two/three-wheelers: Rs. 2500 fee + Rs. 2500 security deposit. (b) Mixed fleets: 50 buses/200 vehicles: Rs. 25000 + Rs. 25000; 51-100 buses/201-500 vehicles: Rs. 50000 + Rs. 50000; 101-200 buses/501-2000 vehicles: Rs. 200000 + Rs. 200000; 200+ buses/2000+ vehicles: Rs. 500000 + Rs. 500000. Duplicate license: Rs. 500. Address change/new branch: Rs. 2500.

forms_added: Form AR-4 — Application for Transfer of License (Rule 14a)
notifications.notes: Major amendment to ride-hailing/aggregator regulations in Uttarakhand. Directly relevant to DriveLegal for aggregator compliance queries.

notifications.title: Agents/Canvasser (for the Collection of Passengers and Sales of Tickets for Travelling by Public Service Vehicles) Rules, 2023
notifications.act_under: Section 93, 95 and 96 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
notifications.effective_date: Date of publication in Official Gazette

definitions.agent_canvasser: Any person appointed as such by the owner of public service vehicles on his behalf, engaged in collection of customers or sale of tickets for travel by such vehicle.
definitions.license: A license issued under these rules.
definitions.licensing_authority: State Transport Authority for whole Uttarakhand and Regional Transport Authority for the region.
definitions.travel_agency: Any person, company or firm who owns or has leased vehicles for not less than one year, that arranges journey by road services.
definitions.tour_operator: Person, company or firm having own personal vehicle or lease vehicle for not less than one year, to provide transport, accommodation, sightseeing, entertainment and incidental services.

key_rules.title: Requirement of License
key_rules.content: No person shall act as agent/canvasser unless licensed from the concerned Transport Authority. No vehicle owner shall employ any such person without them obtaining the agent's license.

key_rules.title: Validity of License
key_rules.content: 3 years from date of issue or renewal. Effective only in the area or region in which it has been issued or renewed.

key_rules.title: Application for License
key_rules.content: Apply in Form T.R.-1 (written or online) to Licensing Authority. Fee as per Rule 22. Required documents: copy of vehicle registration and permit; lease agreement if applicable; identity and date of birth certificate; company registration and GST certificate; self-attested office address and map; office rent agreement if applicable.

key_rules.title: Scrutiny Criteria
key_rules.content: Travel agency: minimum 5 own vehicles or 5 on lease for min 1 year + road services. Tour operator: minimum 5 own vehicles or 5 on lease. Good moral character. Office owned or leased with reception hall, administrative section, secured luggage room, drinking water, toilets, parking. Vehicle maintenance facilities. Day and night telephone. Sufficient financial resources.

key_rules.title: Security Deposit
key_rules.content: Bank guarantee from scheduled bank to be deposited at time of grant. Returned on expiry or voluntary cessation of business. May be forfeited in whole or part at discretion of Licensing Authority.

key_rules.title: Issue of License
key_rules.content: Issued on Form T.R.-3 after verification against Rule 6 criteria.

key_rules.title: Renewal
key_rules.content: Application in Form T.R.-4 with fee per Rule 22. Duplicate license application in Form T.R.-5.

key_rules.title: Display of License
key_rules.content: Must carry license while on duty and produce on demand.

key_rules.title: General Conditions
key_rules.content: Cannot contract with vehicles not covered by permit. Must treat passengers courteously. Maintain fully furnished office. Cannot transfer license. Maintain complaint book. Maintain vehicle register in Form T.R.-8. Cannot change principal place of business without permission.

key_rules.title: Agent's Badge
key_rules.content: Rectangular badge (6.5 cm x 4.0 cm) with name, license number, service name, area name. Worn on left chest. Cannot be lent to others.

key_rules.title: Penalty for Violation
key_rules.content: Contravention of any rule or Section 93 of MV Act punishable as per Section 193 of the Act.

key_rules.title: Appeal
key_rules.content: Appeal before State Transport Appellate Tribunal within 30 days of receipt of order.

forms.purpose: Vehicle Register maintained by License Holder

notifications.title: Uttarakhand Road Transport Accident Relief Fund (Amendment) Rules, 2023
notifications.short_title: UK Road Transport Accident Relief Fund (Amendment) Rules, 2023

notifications.effective_date: Date of publication in Official Gazette

amendments.change: Heading 'Entitlement to Relief' replaced with 'Entitlement to Relief and Distribution of Relief Amount'.

New sub-rule added: District Magistrate of the district in whose jurisdiction the accident occurred, after ascertaining that the vehicle involved is a public service vehicle and the identity of persons entitled to relief has been established, shall immediately distribute the relief amount under sub-rule (2) of rule 4 in favour of entitled persons.

amendments.rule: Rule 8(3) — Initial Fund Distribution to Districts
amendments.existing: Within 15 days of coming into force, Rs. 25 lakh placed at disposal of each District Magistrate by Transport Commissioner/Chairman Uttarakhand Road Transport Accident Relief Fund.
amendments.substituted: Within 15 days of coming into force, Rs. 50 lakh placed at disposal of each District Magistrate by Transport Commissioner/Chairman Uttarakhand Road Transport Accident Relief Fund.

amendments.change: Existing rule required District Magistrate to conduct inquiry to ascertain entitlement to relief and ensure disbursement. New rule: District Magistrate shall cause inquiry to identify causes of the accident and obtain suggestions for preventing recurrence of such accidents in future.

amendments.existing: On demand from District Magistrate, Transport Commissioner re-allocates such amount ensuring minimum Rs. 25 lakh balance in DM's savings account.
amendments.substituted: On demand from District Magistrate, Transport Commissioner re-allocates such amount ensuring minimum Rs. 50 lakh balance in DM's savings account.

financial_impact.notes: Minimum per-district accident relief corpus doubled from Rs. 25 lakh to Rs. 50 lakh.
